questions.prompt: Given `const int ci = 7; const int& r = ci; auto x = r;`, what is the deduced type of `x`?
questions.explanation: By-value `auto` follows template parameter deduction (`template<class T> void f(T)`), which strips references first and then discards top-level cv-qualifiers. Therefore `x` is a plain mutable `int`.

questions.prompt: What are the deduced types of `a` and `b` in C++17 and later?
questions.explanation: Since C++17 (N3922), direct-list-initialization `auto a{10};` with a single element deduces `int`, whereas copy-list-initialization `auto b = {10};` continues to deduce `std::initializer_list<int>`.

questions.prompt: What happens when calling `auto& r = bad_return();` on this C++23 function?
options: It returns a dangling reference (`int&`) to destroyed stack variable `local`.
It triggers guaranteed copy elision into the caller's object.
It fails to compile because parentheses around a return operand are forbidden.
questions.explanation: With `decltype(auto)`, `return (local);` applies `decltype((local))`. Because `(local)` is a parenthesized lvalue expression rather than an unparenthesized id-expression, `decltype` yields `int&`, returning a dangling reference to `local`.

questions.prompt: Given `std::vector v1{1, 2, 3};`, what are the types of `v2` and `v3` deduced by CTAD?
questions.explanation: Under [over.match.class.deduct], single-element `std::vector v2{v1}` selects the synthesized copy-deduction candidate, producing `std::vector<int>` as a copy of `v1`. Passing two `v1` arguments in `v3{v1, v1}` cannot match the copy constructor and instead matches `initializer_list<std::vector<int>>`.

questions.prompt: Given `struct S { int x; double y; }; S s{1, 2.0}; auto& [a, b] = s;`, what are `decltype(a)` and `decltype((a))`?
questions.explanation: Under [dcl.type.decltype] and [dcl.struct.bind], `a` is a structured binding rather than a reference variable, so `decltype(a)` yields the referenced member's declared type (`int`). Parenthesizing `(a)` turns it into a general lvalue expression, so `decltype((a))` yields `int&`.

questions.prompt: Given `int arr[4]{};`, why do `auto p = arr;` and `auto& r = arr;` deduce different types?
options: Because `auto` without `&` performs array-to-pointer decay (`int*`), whereas `auto&` binds to the actual array type (`int(&)[4]`).
Because `auto p = arr;` is ill-formed in C++20 unless `arr` is `std::array`.
Because `auto& r = arr;` decays `arr` into a reference to pointer `int*&`.
questions.explanation: By-value template parameter deduction (`template<class T> void f(T)`) applies lvalue-to-rvalue and array-to-pointer decay before deducing `T`, so `auto p = arr;` deduces `int*`. Reference parameter deduction (`template<class T> void g(T&)`) suppresses array decay, so `auto& r = arr;` deduces `int(&)[4]`.
